column1: # NIMCP toxicity classifier — pattern rules (TSV, tab-separated)
# Format (5 tab-separated columns):
#   category   harm_weight   fairness_weight   posix_regex   description
# Categories:
#   - allowlist:                Anti-toxic patterns. ANY match short-circuits
#                               classify() to a clean result (no flag, even if
#                               toxic patterns would otherwise match). Used to
#                               protect explicit anti-toxic speech like "X are
#                               not subhuman" from false-positive flagging.
#   - dehumanization:           Demographic group + dehumanizing predicate.
#   - violence_against_group:   Direct violence call against a group.
#   - slurs_external:           Pseudo-row whose regex is the marker
#                               "__LOAD_FROM_FILE__<path>". The loader sources
#                               additional patterns (one per line) from that
#                               file. Default path: data/safety/slurs.txt
#                               (not shipped — populate from a curated source
#                               like Hatebase before deployment).
# Notes:
#   - Comments start with '#'. Blank lines ignored.
#   - Patterns use POSIX extended regex (REG_EXTENDED | REG_ICASE | REG_NEWLINE).
#   - POSIX ERE does NOT support lookbehind/lookahead, so negation cases
#     ("X are NOT subhuman") are handled via the allowlist short-circuit
#     rather than inline regex negation.
#   - harm_weight populates predicted_harm via max() across matched rules.
#   - fairness_weight populates fairness_violation via max() across matched rules.
#   - These are *seed* rules: conservative, high-precision, low-recall. They
#     intentionally miss subtle/coded toxicity. Pair with an ML model in
#     production.
# Design principle: demographic descriptors below are NEUTRAL words. Toxicity
# comes from the COMBINATION (group + dehumanizing/violent predicate).
##VERSION 2
# ALLOWLIST — anti-toxic constructions. Short-circuits classify() on match.
# "X are/aren't NOT subhuman/inferior/animals/etc." — explicit anti-dehumanization.
# The same predicates that flag in dehumanization category are anti-toxic here
# when preceded by negation.
allowlist
column5: X are not subhuman — anti-dehumanization construction

column1: # "Don't / never / shouldn't" + violence verb + group
allowlist
# DEHUMANIZATION
# Group (singular OR plural, optional "people/folks/men/women" suffix) +
# (are|aren't) + (not real)? + (human|humans) — Class A: "not real humans"
# construction. aren't already encodes negation; "are not real human(s)" too.
dehumanization
column5: X aren't (real) humans — Class A dehumanization (denying personhood)

column1: # Group + are + (sub)human/inferior/animal-class — Class B: explicit dehum.
# predicate. NOTE: the allowlist row above catches the "are not" variant first.
dehumanization
# "X are the cancer/plague/disease of society/world/humanity" — metaphor dehum.
dehumanization
column5: X are the cancer of society — metaphorical dehumanization

column1: # VIOLENCE AGAINST GROUP
# Imperative: kill/gas/deport/etc. + group (with optional "the" / "all" prefix
# and optional " people/folks/men/women" suffix on the group).
violence_against_group
column5: Direct violence imperative against demographic group

column1: # Death-to-group framing
violence_against_group
column5: Death to X — explicit violence call

column1: # Genocide framing
violence_against_group
# "X should (all) be killed/gassed/deported/etc." — passive violence.
# Optional " people/folks" infix between group and "should".
violence_against_group
column5: Group should be killed — passive violence

column1: # Patterns specific to misogynistic language. Distinct from generic violence/
# dehumanization because misogyny has its own linguistic surface: derogation
# (bitches/whores/sluts as group terms), objectification (treat as property/
# object), denial of competence (women can't / belong in kitchen / etc.).
# Allowlist negation forms in the existing allowlist rows already cover
# "women are not X" / "don't kill women" via the irregular-plural enumeration.
# Misogynistic group-derogation: targeting women with sex-derogation terms
# used as group descriptors. Plurals + slur-as-group form. NOTE: these
# terms can appear in non-toxic contexts (reclaimed speech, art); the
# pattern requires the slur to be the grammatical SUBJECT of a derogatory
# predicate to keep precision high.
misogyny
column5: women are X — group + derogatory predicate

column1: # Denial of agency / competence: "women can't" + role/competence verbs;
# "women belong in" + diminished domain.
misogyny
misogyny
# Objectification as property: a woman/wife is X's possession.
misogyny
# Imperative violence against women/girls (overlaps violence_against_group
# but stated separately so the matched_category surfaces as 'misogyny' for
# downstream policy/curriculum routing). Allowlist negation already covers
# "don't rape" etc. via the don't|never|shouldn't prefix.
misogyny
# "Real women" / "real men" purity rhetoric that polices women's
# behavior. Cheap to detect: "real women X" or "a real woman would Y".
misogyny
# "Make me a sandwich" / "get back in the kitchen" as imperatives.
misogyny
column5: Get back in the kitchen — confine-to-domain imperative

column1: # EXTERNAL SLUR LIST (optional)
# Loads one POSIX-extended regex per line from data/safety/slurs.txt if it
# exists. NOT shipped with the repo — populate from a curated source like
# Hatebase (https://hatebase.org/) or Jigsaw's Perspective taxonomy before
# deploying. If the file is missing, this row is silently skipped and the
# classifier still works without slur coverage.
slurs_external
column5: Sourced from external curated slur list (file optional)
